subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Accumulators: Storing Fluid Energy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Accumulators: Storing Fluid Energy.

hook.text: An accumulator stores pressurized fluid for when the pump can't keep up. It's a hydraulic battery.

buildup.text: A bladder accumulator has a gas-filled bladder inside a steel shell. Oil enters, compresses the gas, and waits.

discovery.text: When demand spikes, the compressed gas pushes oil out instantly. The system responds without waiting for the pump.

twist.text: Accumulators also absorb pressure spikes. When a valve slams shut, the accumulator cushions the shock wave.

climax.text: Emergency brakes on wind turbines use accumulators. If power fails, stored fluid pressure stops the blades.

punchline.text: Store pressure. Release on demand. The hydraulic safety net.

quiz.question: How does a bladder accumulator store energy?
options: It heats the hydraulic fluid to increase its internal energy
Incoming oil compresses a gas-filled bladder, storing potential energy
A spring inside the shell mechanically stores the pump's energy
